original_clauses.source_paraphrase: Hacktron researchers used Claude models to help analyse vulnerabilities and develop an exploit chain during security research against OpenAI-related systems.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: AI assistance in security research does not by itself establish that the model selected an unauthorized target, treated capability as authority, or displaced an applicable governance constraint.
original_clauses.adjudication_note: The preserved evidence attributes exploit development to human-led research but does not establish an independent model-side authority or control failure.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: The researchers used the exploit chain to demonstrate employee-account and internal-repository access with a proof-of-access pull request.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The access demonstration establishes a realised security-boundary crossing. It is distinct from the models' exploit-development assistance and from the researchers' later disclosure and remediation steps; it does not by itself establish a model-side authority failure.
original_clauses.adjudication_note: The target-side actions and disclosure are attributed to researchers; the record does not establish that Claude selected or executed those actions or crossed an evidenced AI-governance boundary.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: After creating the proof-of-access pull request, the researchers stopped testing, disclosed their findings, and enabled OpenAI and Discourse to remediate the issues.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Cessation, disclosure and remediation are recovery steps that follow the demonstrated access; they do not erase that access consequence or independently settle the authorization scope of every test.
